lead.headline: Jensen Huang Quits Nvidia, Jolting Chip Stocks as Wall Street Slips
lead.deck: The co-founder's abrupt exit sent Nvidia down as much as 14% before a partial recovery, while rising oil and a 5% Treasury yield kept the broader market on the back foot.
body: Nvidia said Jensen Huang had resigned as president, chief executive and director with immediate effect, ending more than three decades at the helm of the company he co-founded in 1993. The move followed days of reports about his personal conduct and a board review. Chief financial officer Colette Kress was named interim CEO while keeping her finance role, longtime director Harvey Jones became the company's first board chair, and a search for a permanent successor will look at internal and external candidates.

Nvidia shares fell as much as 14% in early trading and touched a 52-week low before closing down 4.34% at $166.19, on volume more than double the recent average. The stock is down about 20% so far in November. Citi cut its price target to $225 from $285. Rival chipmakers AMD and Broadcom each gained more than 5% as investors weighed alternatives, and Nvidia's results, due on 17 November, will now be presented under interim leadership.

The S&P 500 fell 26.98 points, or 0.35%, to 7,592.40, after recovering from an early drop of nearly 1%. The Dow lost 189.40 points to 52,297.09 and the Nasdaq Composite shed 100.10 points to 25,366.09, while the small-cap Russell 2000 dropped about 1.7%. The 10-year Treasury yield held near 5%, with Fed officials continuing to signal that a December rate rise is on the table.

Oil jumped after reports of attacks on Saudi energy facilities and disruption to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, with Brent settling up 3.3% at $95.82. Gold fell nearly 3% to around $3,876 an ounce as yields and the dollar firmed. In India, the rupee weakened 33 paise to 94.04 per dollar, while the Nifty edged up for a third day.

top: Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia's CEO with immediate effect; CFO Colette Kress is interim chief and the stock closed 4.3% lower.
Brent crude jumped 3.3% to $95.82 after attacks on Saudi energy sites, while gold fell nearly 3%.
Hancock Whitney agreed to buy Trustmark in an all-stock deal valued at about $3.2 billion, creating a $58 billion Gulf South lender.
Europe's Stoxx 600 notched a second record close as Burberry jumped about 8% on a sharp profit recovery.
The rupee fell 33 paise to 94.04 per dollar, and Ola Electric's quarterly revenue dropped 39%.

items.headline: Wall Street Pares Losses After Nvidia Shock
items.body: Stocks recovered most of an early slide as energy shares rose with crude. Jobless claims rose to 200,000, slightly above forecasts, and existing home sales fell to their lowest annual pace since 2010.

items.headline: Europe Shrugs Off Chip Sell-Off for Another Record
items.body: Strong results from Burberry, Munich Re and Siemens outweighed losses in semiconductor names such as Infineon, ASML and BE Semiconductor. UK GDP grew 0.7% in the third quarter, in line with expectations.

items.headline: Asia Retreats as Nvidia Turmoil Hits Chip Hubs
items.body: Taiwan's Taiex fell to 43,091.87 and Tokyo ended a three-day winning streak, with chip-linked shares under pressure as Nvidia's leadership crisis unfolded overnight.

items.headline: Dalal Street Edges Higher in a Choppy Session
items.body: Financials and real estate lifted the Nifty for a third day, while autos, FMCG and IT slipped. The rupee weakened as hawkish Fed comments strengthened the dollar.

items.headline: Nvidia Slides as Rivals Rally
items.body: Investors rotated into AMD and Broadcom after Huang's exit, while Apple touched a fresh intraday record. Nvidia's market value hovered just under $4 trillion.

items.headline: Nebius Sinks on Trimmed Outlook
items.body: The AI cloud provider posted quarterly revenue of $980.8 million, up sharply from a year ago, but narrowed its 2026 revenue guidance to $3.0–3.2 billion, citing delays in third-party data-centre capacity, and lifted its spending plans.

items.headline: Burberry Soars, Nissan and Naver Slump
items.body: Burberry's first-half adjusted operating profit more than tripled. In Asia, Nissan fell after a 96% drop in quarterly operating profit and a lower sales forecast, and Naver lost about 6% as AI costs dented its profit.

items.headline: HAL Falls Despite Profit Growth
items.body: Hindustan Aeronautics slipped even after a 16% rise in quarterly profit, and Aurobindo Pharma extended losses after a US FDA warning on a subsidiary's plant. HDFC Life and Shriram Finance led Nifty gainers.

items.headline: Hancock Whitney to Buy Trustmark
items.body: The deal would create a regional bank with about $58 billion in assets across six southeastern US states. Hancock Whitney holders would own about 65% of the combined company, with closing expected late in the first quarter of 2027.

items.headline: Komatsu Buys Astec's Road Equipment Arm
items.body: Astec Industries agreed to sell its road construction equipment business, including the Roadtec and Carlson brands, to Komatsu America.

items.headline: PAI Pharma Adds Hospital Injectables Maker Nexus
items.body: PAI Pharma acquired Nexus Pharmaceuticals to expand its range of injectable medicines for hospitals, while Sweden's ASSA ABLOY agreed to buy Brazilian aluminium products maker Rometal.

items.headline: Nvidia Commits to Bigger Anthropic Stake After IPO
items.body: An amended prospectus showed Nvidia has agreed to buy another $10 billion of Anthropic stock immediately after the AI company's listing, expected next week.

items.headline: Citadel Becomes No. 2 Holder in Hankyu Hanshin
items.body: Ken Griffin's firm disclosed the position in the Osaka-based railway and property group via its semiannual report, without stating its intentions. The shares rose as much as 3.7% in Tokyo.

items.headline: Funds Pile Into Shorts on Big Tech
items.body: A crowding report covering more than 700 hedge funds found managers added short positions in Amazon, Apple, Nvidia and Meta in October, with Apple's positioning at its weakest of the year. Tesla was the only Magnificent Seven stock to see fewer short holders.

items.headline: Prime Brokers Open Door to Prediction Markets
items.body: Clear Street and Marex are preparing to give institutional clients access to Kalshi's event contracts, a sign of Wall Street's growing interest in prediction-market trading.

items.headline: Ola Electric's Sales Shrink Again
items.body: The EV maker's quarterly revenue fell sharply as registrations dropped 17%, though its loss narrowed 13%. Separately, the consumer regulator fined ride-hailing app Ola ₹10 lakh over an advance-tipping feature it called a dark pattern.

items.headline: Consumer and Climate Startups Raise Fresh Capital
items.body: Amazon's Smbhav and Climate Pledge funds co-led Greenjoules' Series B, while Titan Capital led a first institutional round for Mumbai's bootstrapped Hundo Pizza. Jaipur menswear label QB MEN raised a pre-seed round led by BeyondSeed.

items.headline: Reliance Plans Coal Gasification Project
items.body: Reliance Industries announced a coal gasification project in Andhra Pradesh, which it expects to create about 40,000 jobs.

items.headline: Unacademy Changes CEO; Norwest Closes Record Fund
items.body: Gaurav Munjal moves to executive chairman at Unacademy, with chief business officer Akhilendra Kumar taking over as CEO after its acquisition by upGrad. Venture firm Norwest closed its largest fund yet.
